egin{example} \end{example}[Zero shape operator and hyperplanes]

Source: petersen:page-0114, petersen:page-0115 ↗ def:pet-ch3-distance-function-notation 1. ch3:3.2.9Let $H\subset \mathbb R^n$ be an orientable hypersurface with unit normal $N$ and shape operator $S(v)= abla _vN$. If $S=0$ on $H$, $N$ is constant on $H$ and $H$ is open in the hyperplane $\{ x+p\mid x\cdot N_p=0\} $ for fixed $p\in H$. Explicitly, for the isometric immersion $(x^1,\dots ,x^{n-1})\mapsto (c(x^1),x^2,\dots ,x^{n-1})$ of a unit-speed curve $c$ into $\mathbb R^n$, the unit normal is $N=(-\dot c^2(x^1),\dot c^1(x^1),0,\dots ,0)$, and $S\equiv 0$ iff $\ddot c^1\equiv \ddot c^2\equiv 0$ iff $c$ is a straight line iff $H$ is open in a hyperplane. \end{example}
Proof

↗ ex:pet-ch3-zero-shape-operator-hyperplane \sketch For the displayed immersion,

\[ abla N=(-\ddot c^2\partial _1+\ddot c^1\partial _2)\, dx^1. \]

Hence $S=0$ exactly when $c$ is a straight line. In general, $S=0$ makes the unit normal constant on each connected component, so the hypersurface lies openly in the corresponding affine hyperplane; the converse is immediate.

□
